cards.explanation: The answer is the king of Egypt. Neco, king of Egypt, makes Eliakim, the brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 36:4). Egypt took the old king off the throne and then picked the next one too (2 Chronicles 36:3). A different hand put the crown on this time than in verse 1, friends.

The answer is Egypt. Neco, king of Egypt, takes Jehoahaz and carries him off there (2 Chronicles 36:4). Jehoahaz had been Judah's king, and now he's headed to Egypt with Neco. That's a rough commute, friends.

The answer is False. Jehoiakim doesn't do what is right. The text says he "…did evil in the sight of the LORD his God." (2 Chronicles 36:5). Later the text says his abominations, and all that was found against him, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah (2 Chronicles 36:8).

The answer is some articles from the house of the LORD. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, takes some of the articles from the house of the LORD to Babylon (2 Chronicles 36:7). The house of the LORD is the temple in Jerusalem. He had bound Jehoiakim to take him to Babylon (2 Chronicles 36:6), and now he takes things from that holy place too.

The answer is False, friends. The text says Nebuchadnezzar put the articles "…in his temple in Babylon." (2 Chronicles 36:7). It's a temple, not a palace. One little word, and it changes where those articles landed.

The answer is True. The text says Jehoiachin "…did evil in the sight of the LORD…" (2 Chronicles 36:9). He's the son of Jehoiakim, and he reigned in his father's place (2 Chronicles 36:8). Another king, friends, and the verdict is the same.

The answer is three. Jehoiachin reigns three months and ten days (2 Chronicles 36:9). That's about as short as the reign of Jehoahaz, who also gets three months (2 Chronicles 36:2). Not much time to even find where the good chairs are.

The answer is King Nebuchadnezzar. The king of Babylon is the one who makes Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 36:10). Zedekiah is Jehoiachin's relative. Judah's throne is now being handed out by Babylon, friends.

The answer is False. Zedekiah, the king, "…did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke for the LORD." (2 Chronicles 36:12). Jeremiah was a prophet speaking for the LORD, and the king didn't humble himself before him. I think that's a hard way to listen to a message.

The answer is that he rebels against him. Zedekiah rebels against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God (2 Chronicles 36:13). Nebuchadnezzar is the king he turned on. The text also says he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to the LORD, the God of Israel.

The answer is that He has compassion on them. The text says the LORD sent word to His people again and again "…because He had compassion on them and on His dwelling place." (2 Chronicles 36:15). Think about that, friends. After all those evil deeds, He was still sending word. That's the heart behind every messenger.

The answer is that they mock and scoff at them. The text says, "But they mocked the messengers of God, despising His words and scoffing at His prophets…" (2 Chronicles 36:16). I think that's a hard thing to read, because the messengers kept coming and the people kept laughing at them. It's a sad line, friends.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar. The text says "God gave them all into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar…" (2 Chronicles 36:17). He's the king of Babylon we've been following all chapter, and the king of the Chaldeans in this verse is him. His name keeps coming up for a reason.

The answer is True. The text says "…the Chaldeans set fire to the house of God and broke down the wall of Jerusalem." (2 Chronicles 36:19). This is a heavy part of the story, friends. The house of God, burned.

The answer is Persia. The exiles served Nebuchadnezzar and his sons "…until the kingdom of Persia came to power." (2 Chronicles 36:20). That's a long wait with a clear end. And it connects right to Cyrus, king of Persia, a few verses later.

The answer is Jeremiah. The land enjoyed its Sabbath rest until seventy years were completed, "…in fulfillment of the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah." (2 Chronicles 36:21). He's the same prophet Zedekiah wouldn't humble himself before (2 Chronicles 36:12). The word he spoke for the LORD came true, friends.

The answer is the LORD. The text says "…the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia to send a proclamation throughout his kingdom…" (2 Chronicles 36:22). Cyrus is a king of Persia, and the LORD is the one who moved him. This happened to fulfill the word spoken through Jeremiah.

The answer is to build Him a house at Jerusalem. Cyrus says the LORD "…has appointed me to build a house for Him at Jerusalem in Judah." (2 Chronicles 36:23). A house for the LORD, in Jerusalem. After the house of God was burned, that's a big announcement, friends.

The answer is True. Cyrus says, "Whoever among you belongs to His people, may the LORD his God be with him, and may he go up." (2 Chronicles 36:23). Exiles who had been servants in Babylon hear the door open. That's a big change, friends.
